services.name: AWS IAM
services.what: Controls who can sign in to AWS and what each user, group, role or service is allowed to do, using permission policies.

services.name: AWS IAM Identity Center
services.what: Gives your workforce one sign-in to many AWS accounts and business apps, using users from your own identity provider or its built-in directory.

services.name: AWS STS
services.what: Issues short-lived credentials, for example when a user or service assumes an IAM role or signs in through federation.

services.name: AWS Organizations
services.what: Groups many AWS accounts under one management account, with consolidated billing and policies, such as SCPs, that limit what the accounts can do.

services.name: AWS Control Tower
services.what: Sets up and governs a multi-account AWS environment (a landing zone) on top of Organizations, with ready-made guardrails and automatic account creation.

services.name: AWS RAM
services.what: Shares resources such as subnets, transit gateways or Route 53 Resolver rules with other accounts, without copying them.

services.name: Amazon Cognito
services.what: Adds sign-up and sign-in to web and mobile apps (user pools) and gives app users temporary AWS credentials (identity pools).

services.name: AWS Directory Service
services.what: Runs Microsoft Active Directory on AWS (AWS Managed Microsoft AD), or connects AWS to the directory you already run on premises (AD Connector).

services.name: AWS KMS
services.what: Creates and controls the encryption keys that AWS services use to encrypt your data, and logs every use of them in CloudTrail.

services.name: AWS CloudHSM
services.what: Dedicated hardware security modules in your VPC that only you control, for encryption keys that must stay in single-tenant, FIPS-validated hardware.

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.what: Stores database passwords, API keys and other secrets, and can rotate them automatically on a schedule.

services.name: AWS Certificate Manager
services.what: Issues, stores and renews SSL/TLS certificates for AWS services such as load balancers, CloudFront and API Gateway.

services.name: AWS Private CA
services.what: Runs your own private certificate authority, to issue certificates for internal services, devices and users.

services.name: AWS WAF
services.what: A web application firewall that inspects HTTP(S) requests to CloudFront, load balancers, API Gateway and other services, and blocks them by rules such as IP lists, rate limits or SQL injection checks.

services.name: AWS Shield
services.what: Protects against DDoS attacks: Shield Standard is automatic and free, and Shield Advanced adds stronger protection, a response team and cost protection.

services.name: AWS Firewall Manager
services.what: Applies WAF rules, Shield Advanced protection, security groups and Network Firewall policies across all the accounts in an organization from one place.

services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
services.what: Detects threats by continuously analyzing CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and other activity for signs of compromise.

services.name: Amazon Inspector
services.what: Automatically scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

services.name: Amazon Macie
services.what: Uses machine learning to find and report sensitive data, such as personal information, stored in S3 buckets.

services.name: Amazon Detective
services.what: Helps investigate security findings by linking logs and events into graphs that show what happened and which resources were involved.

services.name: AWS Security Hub
services.what: Gathers security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and other tools in one place, and checks accounts against security best-practice standards.

services.name: AWS Audit Manager
services.what: Continuously collects evidence from your AWS usage to help you prepare for audits against standards such as PCI DSS or GDPR.

services.name: Amazon VPC
services.what: Your own isolated network in AWS, with the subnets, route tables, gateways and security rules that you define.

services.name: Amazon VPC Lattice
services.what: Connects, secures and monitors traffic between services across VPCs and accounts, without managing load balancers or network peering.

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.what: Lets a VPC reach an AWS service, or a service in another VPC, through private IP addresses in its own subnets (interface endpoints), without the internet.

services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
services.what: A regional hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks, so each one attaches once instead of peering with every other network.

services.name: AWS Direct Connect
services.what: A dedicated private network connection from your data center or office to AWS, with more consistent performance than the internet.

services.name: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
services.what: Encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet between your on-premises network and a VPC or transit gateway.

services.name: AWS Client VPN
services.what: A managed VPN that lets individual users connect securely from their own devices to AWS and on-premises networks.

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.what: Spreads incoming traffic across healthy targets such as EC2 instances, containers or IP addresses; it comes as Application, Network and Gateway Load Balancers.

services.name: Application Load Balancer
services.what: A load balancer for HTTP and HTTPS traffic (layer 7) that can route each request by its path, host name or headers.

services.name: Network Load Balancer
services.what: A load balancer for TCP, UDP and TLS traffic (layer 4), built for very high throughput, low latency and static IP addresses.

services.name: Gateway Load Balancer
services.what: Sends traffic through a fleet of third-party virtual appliances, such as firewalls, and spreads the load across them.

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.what: A DNS service that registers domain names and directs users to your resources, with health checks and routing policies such as latency, weighted or failover.

services.name: Amazon Route 53 Resolver
services.what: Answers DNS queries inside a VPC; its inbound and outbound endpoints and forwarding rules connect DNS between AWS and on-premises networks.

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.what: A content delivery network (CDN) that caches your content and serves it from edge locations close to users around the world.

services.name: Lambda@Edge
services.what: Runs Lambda functions at CloudFront locations to change requests and responses, for example to rewrite URLs or add headers.

services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
services.what: Gives an application two static anycast IP addresses and carries users' traffic over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy endpoint.

services.name: AWS Network Firewall
services.what: A managed, stateful network firewall and intrusion prevention service that filters traffic going in and out of your VPCs.

services.name: AWS Local Zones
services.what: Extensions of an AWS Region in large cities, so selected services run close to the users there with single-digit-millisecond latency.

services.name: AWS Wavelength
services.what: AWS compute and storage placed inside telecom carriers' 5G networks, for apps that need very low latency to mobile devices.

services.name: Amazon EC2
services.what: Virtual servers (instances) in the cloud that you choose the size of, configure and pay for while they run.

services.name: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
services.what: Adds or removes EC2 instances in a group automatically to match demand, and replaces instances that fail health checks.

services.name: Application Auto Scaling
services.what: Scales resources other than EC2 instances, such as ECS services, DynamoDB capacity, Aurora replicas and Lambda provisioned concurrency.

services.name: AWS Auto Scaling
services.what: Builds scaling plans that scale several related resources, such as EC2 Auto Scaling groups and DynamoDB tables, together.

services.name: EC2 Image Builder
services.what: Automates building, testing and distributing up-to-date AMIs and container images on a schedule.

services.name: Instance Scheduler on AWS
services.what: An AWS solution that stops and starts EC2 and RDS instances on schedules you set, so they don't run when nobody needs them.

services.name: AMI
services.what: A template holding an operating system and software, which EC2 uses to launch instances.

services.name: Amazon Linux
services.what: AWS's own Linux operating system, tuned for EC2 and kept up to date with security fixes by AWS.

services.name: AWS Graviton
services.what: Arm-based processors designed by AWS, used in many EC2 instance types and in Lambda, for better price performance.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.what: Runs your code in response to events without any servers to manage, and charges only for the time the code runs.

services.name: Amazon ECS
services.what: Runs and manages containers, either on EC2 instances you manage or serverless with Fargate.

services.name: Amazon EKS
services.what: Runs Kubernetes for you, so containerized applications can be deployed with standard Kubernetes tools on EC2 or Fargate.

services.name: AWS Load Balancer Controller
services.what: A Kubernetes add-on that creates Application and Network Load Balancers for the services and ingresses in an EKS cluster.

services.name: AWS Fargate
services.what: Runs containers for ECS and EKS without you managing any servers or clusters of EC2 instances.

services.name: Amazon ECR
services.what: A private registry that stores, scans and shares your container images.

services.name: AWS Batch
services.what: Runs large numbers of batch computing jobs, queuing them and providing the right amount of compute for them automatically.

services.name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
services.what: Deploys and runs web applications for you: you upload the code, and it sets up the servers, load balancing, scaling and monitoring.

services.name: AWS Outposts
services.what: AWS-managed racks or servers installed in your own data center that run AWS services on premises.

services.name: Amazon Lightsail
services.what: Simple virtual servers with storage and networking bundled at a fixed monthly price, for small websites and applications.

services.name: Amazon S3
services.what: Object storage for any amount of data, kept as objects in buckets and reached over HTTPS, with storage classes from frequent access to long-term archive.

services.name: Amazon EBS
services.what: Block storage volumes attached to EC2 instances over the network, like virtual hard drives that keep their data when an instance stops.

services.name: Amazon EFS
services.what: A shared NFS file system for Linux that grows and shrinks automatically and that many instances can mount at once.

services.name: Amazon FSx
services.what: Fully managed file systems built on popular products: Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS.

services.name: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
services.what: Managed Windows file shares over SMB, joined to Active Directory, for Windows applications and users.

services.name: Amazon FSx for Lustre
services.what: A managed high-performance file system for compute-heavy work such as HPC and machine learning, which can be linked to an S3 bucket.

services.name: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
services.what: Managed NetApp ONTAP file systems reached over NFS, SMB and iSCSI, with ONTAP features such as snapshots, replication and data tiering.

services.name: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
services.what: Managed OpenZFS file systems over NFS, with fast snapshots and clones, for moving Linux ZFS workloads to AWS.

services.name: AWS Storage Gateway
services.what: A hybrid service that gives on-premises applications cloud storage through a local file, volume or tape gateway that caches recent data.

services.name: AWS Backup
services.what: Schedules, stores and manages backups across AWS services such as EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and S3 from one place.

services.name: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager
services.what: Automatically creates, keeps, copies and deletes EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs on a schedule.

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.what: Moves large amounts of data online between on-premises storage, other clouds and AWS storage services, with scheduling and integrity checks.

services.name: AWS Transfer Family
services.what: Managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2 servers that store the transferred files directly in S3 or EFS.

services.name: AWS Snowball
services.what: Rugged storage and compute devices that AWS ships to you, to move large amounts of data into AWS offline or to work at remote sites.

services.name: Amazon RDS
services.what: Managed relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and Db2), with backups, patching and failover handled for you.

services.name: Amazon RDS Proxy
services.what: A managed database proxy that pools and shares connections to RDS and Aurora, so many clients at once don't overwhelm the database.

services.name: Amazon Aurora
services.what: A MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database built for the cloud, with its storage copied six ways across three Availability Zones.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.what: A serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit-millisecond performance at any scale.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator
services.what: An in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB that cuts read times from milliseconds to microseconds with few code changes.

services.name: Amazon ElastiCache
services.what: Managed in-memory caches and data stores using Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached, for sub-millisecond reads.

services.name: Amazon Neptune
services.what: A managed graph database for highly connected data, such as social networks, recommendations and fraud detection.

services.name: Amazon DocumentDB
services.what: A managed document database for JSON data that is compatible with MongoDB.

services.name: Amazon Keyspaces
services.what: A serverless managed database compatible with Apache Cassandra and its CQL query language.

services.name: Amazon Redshift
services.what: A managed data warehouse for fast SQL analytics over large amounts of structured data.

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.what: A managed message queue: one part of an application leaves messages, and another picks them up later at its own pace.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.what: A publish/subscribe service that pushes each message to many subscribers at once, such as SQS queues, Lambda functions, email or SMS.

services.name: Amazon EventBridge
services.what: A serverless event bus that routes events from AWS services, your applications and SaaS partners to targets by rules; EventBridge Scheduler runs tasks on a schedule.

services.name: AWS Step Functions
services.what: Joins steps, such as Lambda functions and AWS service calls, into a visual workflow with retries, branching and error handling.

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.what: Creates, publishes and secures REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs in front of Lambda functions or other backends.

services.name: Amazon MQ
services.what: A managed message broker for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ, for applications that already use those brokers.

services.name: AWS AppSync
services.what: A managed GraphQL API service that lets apps query and update data from many sources, with real-time updates.

services.name: Amazon SES
services.what: Sends and receives email at scale, such as notifications, receipts and marketing messages.

services.name: Amazon Kinesis
services.what: A family of services for collecting and processing streaming data in real time, including Kinesis Data Streams and Kinesis Video Streams.

services.name: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
services.what: Captures and stores streaming data, such as clickstreams or IoT readings, in shards that your own applications read in real time.

services.name: Amazon Data Firehose
services.what: Delivers streaming data to destinations such as S3, Redshift or OpenSearch, batching and converting it on the way, with nothing to manage.

services.name: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
services.what: Runs Apache Flink applications that process and analyze streaming data in real time.

services.name: Amazon MSK
services.full: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
services.what: Runs Apache Kafka clusters for you, including a serverless option, for applications built on Kafka.

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.what: Runs SQL queries directly on data in S3 with no servers to manage, charging by the amount of data scanned.

services.name: AWS Glue
services.what: A serverless data integration service that discovers data with crawlers, records it in the Data Catalog and runs ETL jobs.

services.name: AWS Glue DataBrew
services.what: A visual tool for cleaning and preparing data without writing code, using hundreds of ready-made transformations.

services.name: Amazon EMR
services.what: Runs big data frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop on managed clusters or serverless, for large-scale data processing.

services.name: AWS Lake Formation
services.what: Builds and secures data lakes on S3, with permissions down to columns and rows for services such as Athena and Redshift.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
services.what: Managed OpenSearch clusters for full-text search, log analytics and dashboards.

services.name: Amazon QuickSight
services.what: A business intelligence service for building interactive dashboards and reports from your data.

services.name: Amazon Managed Grafana
services.what: Managed Grafana workspaces for visualizing metrics, logs and traces from many data sources in dashboards.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker AI
services.what: Builds, trains and deploys machine learning models, with managed notebooks, training jobs and model hosting.

services.name: Amazon Textract
services.what: Uses machine learning to pull printed and handwritten text, forms and tables out of scanned documents.

services.name: Amazon Comprehend
services.what: Uses natural language processing to find meaning in text, such as sentiment, key phrases, entities and personal data.

services.name: AWS Amplify
services.what: Tools and hosting for building and deploying full-stack web and mobile apps, with sign-in, data and storage built in.

services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
services.what: Collects metrics and logs from AWS resources and applications, with alarms and dashboards to keep watch on them.

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.what: Records the API calls made in your AWS accounts (who did what, when and from where) for auditing and investigation.

services.name: AWS Config
services.what: Records how your resources are configured over time and checks them against rules, flagging any that don't comply.

services.name: AWS Systems Manager
services.what: A set of tools for operating EC2 instances and on-premises servers at scale, such as patching, running commands, remote sessions and storing parameters.

services.name: Systems Manager Parameter Store
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: stores configuration values and secrets as named parameters, optionally encrypted with KMS.

services.name: Systems Manager Session Manager
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: opens a secure shell on instances from the browser or CLI, with no SSH keys, bastion hosts or open inbound ports.

services.name: Systems Manager Patch Manager
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: scans instances for missing patches and installs them on a schedule.

services.name: Systems Manager Run Command
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: runs scripts or commands on many instances at once, without logging in to each one.

services.name: Systems Manager State Manager
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: keeps instances in a configuration you define, applying it again on a schedule.

services.name: Systems Manager Automation
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: runs step-by-step runbooks that automate common operations and fixes across your resources.

services.name: Systems Manager Inventory
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: collects details of the software, settings and files on your instances.

services.name: Systems Manager Maintenance Windows
services.what: Part of Systems Manager: sets the time slots in which tasks such as patching may run on your instances.

services.name: AWS CloudFormation
services.what: Creates and updates AWS resources from templates (infrastructure as code), managed together as a stack you can repeat or roll back.

services.name: CloudFormation StackSets
services.what: Deploys the same CloudFormation stack to many accounts and Regions in one operation.

services.name: AWS CDK
services.what: Defines AWS infrastructure in programming languages such as TypeScript or Python and turns it into CloudFormation templates.

services.name: AWS Service Catalog
services.what: Lets administrators publish approved products, built from CloudFormation templates, that users can then launch themselves.

services.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
services.what: Checks your accounts against AWS best practices for cost, security, fault tolerance, performance and service quotas.

services.name: AWS Health
services.what: Tells you about AWS events that affect your accounts and resources, such as outages or scheduled maintenance, in the Health Dashboard.

services.name: AWS X-Ray
services.what: Traces requests as they pass through your application's services, showing where time is spent and where errors happen.

services.name: Service Quotas
services.what: Shows the limits (quotas) on your AWS resources and lets you request increases.

services.name: AWS License Manager
services.what: Tracks and controls software licenses, such as Microsoft or Oracle ones, across AWS and on-premises servers.

services.name: AWS Compute Optimizer
services.what: Analyzes how resources are used and recommends better-sized EC2 instances, EBS volumes, Lambda functions and more.

services.name: AWS Well-Architected
services.what: AWS's design guidance, plus a free review tool, for building workloads that are secure, reliable, efficient, cost-effective and sustainable.

services.name: AWS Management Console
services.what: The web interface for using and managing AWS services in a browser.

services.name: AWS CLI
services.what: A command-line tool for controlling AWS services from a terminal or a script.

services.name: AWS SDKs
services.what: Libraries for languages such as Python, Java and JavaScript that let your code call AWS services.

services.name: AWS Application Migration Service
services.what: Replicates your servers to AWS continuously and launches them as EC2 instances when you're ready to switch over.

services.name: AWS Migration Hub
services.what: One place to plan and track application migrations to AWS; its Orchestrator automates migration workflows.

services.name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
services.what: Continuously replicates servers to AWS so they can be launched there within minutes if the original site fails.

services.name: Amazon Application Recovery Controller
services.what: Checks whether an application is ready to fail over and shifts its traffic between Regions or Availability Zones with highly reliable controls.

services.name: AWS DMS
services.what: Moves and continuously replicates data between databases, including between different engines, while the source stays in use.

services.name: AWS SCT
services.what: Converts a database's schema and code, such as stored procedures, from one engine to another before the data is moved.

services.name: AWS Cost Explorer
services.what: Charts your AWS costs and usage over time by service, account or tag, and forecasts future spending.

services.name: AWS Budgets
services.what: Sets cost or usage budgets and alerts you, or takes actions, when spending exceeds or is forecast to exceed them.

services.name: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
services.what: Uses machine learning to spot unusual spending and alerts you with its likely cause.

services.name: AWS Cost and Usage Report
services.what: The most detailed record of your AWS costs and usage, delivered as files to an S3 bucket for analysis.

services.name: AWS Cost Optimization Hub
services.what: Gathers cost-saving recommendations, such as rightsizing and Savings Plans, from across your accounts in one place.

services.name: AWS Billing Conductor
services.what: Creates custom billing views and rates, for example to show each customer or team its own adjusted bill.

services.name: AWS Pricing Calculator
services.what: A free web tool for estimating what an AWS architecture will cost before you build it.

services.name: AWS Marketplace
services.what: A catalog where you can find, buy and deploy third-party software and services that run on AWS.

services.name: AWS Support
services.what: AWS's technical support plans: the free Basic plan, and paid plans that add faster responses and expert guidance.

services.name: ARN
services.what: The unique identifier of an AWS resource, used in policies and API calls.
